newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fall in Japan interest rates excessive-govt source.
newsitem.headline: Fall in Japan interest rates excessive-govt source.

text.p: Recent declines in Japanese long-term interest rates are excessive, taking into account economic conditions, a government source said on Tuesday.

"Looking at the present state of the economy and its short-term outlook, a record low level of around 2.1 percent is clearly excessive," the source said, referring to the current level of the yield on the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond.
The source said capital spending remained firm and production was on a rising trend despite a fall in public expenditure.
"The fact that long-term interest rates are on a falling trend clearly deviates from the state of the economy," he said.
The source said the risk of economic growth slowing down significantly in the April to June period may not be as great as expected, looking at recent movements in production.

A Finance Ministry official said although he could not comment on movements of long-term interest rates, he added that the likelihood of economic growth coming to a halt in the April to June quarter was very slim.
"We expect the economy to get back on a clear growth track in the latter half of the year," the official said.
